title: Redwood discovery - reliability & multi-region fallbacks - Hyperion Systems
summary: Discovery focused on reliability and incident tolerance for Hyperion's customer-facing LLM features. Discussed multi-region failover, model fallbacks, SLA targets, and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Agreed next steps: POC benchmark, security docs, pricing, and architecture diagram.
next_steps: Alex Chen: Send pricing sheet and dedicated capacity options by 2027-09-22
Samira Patel: Share benchmark plan and checklist for POC by 2027-09-20
Redwood: Upload SOC2 + security pack link and KMS integration notes
Schedule technical deep dive with SREs (Priya/Javier) week of 2027-09-27
action_items: Alex Chen: Email pricing + contract starter (due 2027-09-22)
Samira Patel: Draft POC test cases for latency/throughput/failover (due 2027-09-20)
Priya Singh/Hyperion: Provide traffic profile and percentiles CSV (due 2027-09-24)
Javier Morales/Hyperion: Provide model prompts and critical flows for quality gating (due 2027-09-24)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can folks introduce themselves real quick?
[00:08] Mike Torres: Mike here, CTO at Hyperion. We're focused on bringing LLM features into our customer portal, so reliability is huge for us.
[00:15] Priya Singh: Priya, SRE lead. We own uptime and incident response for the portal.
[00:20] Javier Morales: Javier, head of ML, i'll be driving the model side and quality metrics.
[00:25] Leah Kim: Leah, product, here for success criteria and rollout timelines.
[00:30] Alex Chen: Great. Samira from Redwood will cover technical fallbacks and options.
[00:35] Samira Patel: hi all, glad to be here. Quick agenda: understand your availability / target SLOs, where you'll host (cloud regions), and what failure modes you want covered—region failures, model/container failures, and network flaps.
[00:48] Mike Torres: For SLOs we currently target 99.95% for user-facing API calls. If that means moving to dedicated infra we need to know costs. Also multi-region is a requirement — our EU customers must not see more than 300ms additional latency.
[01:05] Samira Patel: Understood. A couple quick clarifications: is that 99.95% end-to-end or specifically for inference latency?
[01:12] Leah Kim: End-to-end. User-perceived. But we can break down: 95th and 99th percentile latency are what we really care about.
[01:18] Samira Patel: Good. Redwood has a few levers: Hosted API (fast to onboard), Dedicated pools (reserved GPU with committed throughput), and Private (VPC/air-gapped). All support multi-region routing and automatic fallback policies, but the guarantees differ.
[01:31] Priya Singh: What's the difference in failover behavior between Hosted and Dedicated?
[01:36] Samira Patel: Hosted has automatic routing across regions where we run capacity; we can failover to a healthy region within our control plane. For Dedicated, you can configure region pairs or active-active in your dedicated pools, giving you lower variance and predictable throughput. Private gives you full control but we'd provide the control plane for routing; failover would be your ops-run playbook unless we deploy cross-region private clusters.
[01:53] Javier Morales: On model-level failures, can we fallback to a smaller/cheaper model automatically if the primary model has a degraded node group?
[01:59] Samira Patel: Yes, we support model-variant fallbacks. You can define a policy: primary model on A100, fallback to quantized 8-bit LLM or a smaller architecture in the same family. We also support cache-first flows — if prefix/KV cache hits, we return from cache without hitting the model which helps in spike scenarios.
[02:18] Mike Torres: What's the typical RTO for a region failover? We need to understand user impact in those minutes after a fail.
[02:25] Samira Patel: For Hosted, median detection+reroute is ~20-90 seconds depending on the failure signal (we use a combination of active health checks and control-plane telemetry). For Dedicated with active-active, it's sub-20s for routing at our layer, but if you need your data plane warmed (KV cache, referential state) you can expect some degradation until caches repopulate.
[02:40] Priya Singh: And the cache warm-up is our issue to handle? Can Redwood pre-warm KV cache across regions?
[02:46] Samira Patel: We offer optional pre-warm strategies as an add-on for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we do opportunistic pre-warm for high-traffic prefixes but cannot guarantee cross-region warm cache. You can also ship a prewarm script as part of the POC to target critical prefixes.
[02:58] Alex Chen: We should also talk about canary deployments and rollbacks — those help reduce blast radius during deploys.
[03:05] Samira Patel: Right — Redwood Console supports canaries, A/B rollout, and automatic rollback on error rates or regression in quality metrics. You can bind your eval suite — if responses fail quality gates, we roll back automatically.
[03:16] Javier Morales: That's important — quality regressions are a blocker for ML. If a canary fails our evals, can it automatically fail back to the previous model without human intervention?
[03:24] Samira Patel: Yes, with a policy. You give us thresholds: latency, error rate, and eval pass rate (you upload prompts/evals). If thresholds breach, the control plane triggers rollback and, optionally, a fallback to a pre-approved variant.
[03:35] Mike Torres: How about legal / compliance — in a region outage can data move cross-border? We have EU data residency constraints.
[03:42] Samira Patel: Data residency is configurable. For Hosted we can ensure traffic from EU customers is served from EU regions and we don't persist cross-border logs if you opt out. For Dedicated and Private, you can pin workloads to region-only pools. We'll document the flow for audit.
[03:56] Leah Kim: Are audit logs and KMS integrations available? We need key management and HSM options.
[04:02] Samira Patel: Yes — KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) are supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS for higher tiers. We also provide audit logs for requests, routing decisions, and model rollouts.
[04:12] Priya Singh: On SLAs — do you offer an SLA for Hosted?
[04:15] Samira Patel: Hosted has our standard published SLA at 99.9% for the free tier — for enterprise customers we can offer SLA-backed Dedicated capacity with higher uptime commitments (99.95%+), depending on contract and region coverage.
[04:26] Mike Torres: So to hit 99.95% we likely need Dedicated with active-active?
[04:30] Samira Patel: Generally yes; Dedicated with active-active pools or a Private multi-region setup gives you better tail guarantees. We also recommend coupling with prefix caching and a fallback model to reduce user-visible errors.
[04:40] Sam W.: A quick infra question: how does Redwood handle stateful caches — are they replicated?
[04:46] Samira Patel: KV cache is per-region by default; for Dedicated we offer replication strategies or sticky routing so that most user traffic goes to the same warmed region. Cross-region replication is an add-on due to egress and consistency tradeoffs.
[04:58] Javier Morales: For the POC, we want to run simulated region outage tests and model degradation tests. Can Redwood simulate failures?
[05:05] Samira Patel: Yes, in our staging environment we can run chaos tests: region failover, node kill, and deliberate latency injection. We'll provide runbooks and a failure injection harness.
[05:14] Alex Chen: Great — I'll capture that as a POC item.
[05:18] Mike Torres: Another concern is costs — if we fallback to a larger region or replica in another region, egress and compute costs could spike. How are we billed in outage scenarios?
[05:27] Samira Patel: Billing follows usage; for Dedicated you have committed capacity which mitigates burst costs. Host fallback to other regions may incur cross-region egress. We can set policy caps or automatic throttles to avoid runaway egress. Part of POC is to baseline cost impact of failovers.
[05:40] Priya Singh: We need to ensure incident timelines — who owns the initial failover? Do you trigger and do you notify us?
[05:47] Samira Patel: Our control plane triggers routing changes automatically. We'll send incident notifications and integrate with your PagerDuty and Slack. For Dedicated & Private we offer optional runbook automation and a joint incident bridge with your SREs.
[05:58] Leah Kim: On timelines, our target is to have a pilot by end of Q4 and production roll by Q1. Does that align?
[06:04] Alex Chen: Seems achievable. Samira, is there anything Hyperion needs to prepare for the POC?
[06:09] Samira Patel: We'll need: traffic profile (percentiles), list of critical prompts/flows, performance requirements (p50/p95/p99 targets), and region coverage. Also any compliance docs (SOC2 etc) so we can scope Private if needed.
[06:21] Javier Morales: We'll share prompts and quality gating metrics.
[06:24] Priya Singh: We'll export traffic histograms and spike patterns from the last 90 days.
[06:28] Alex Chen: Cool — we'll include that in the action items.
[06:32] Mike Torres: A more technical question — does Redwood support gradient backoff or queueing during spikes to protect the model?
[06:40] Samira Patel: Yes, Redwood has adaptive throttling and request queuing. For Dedicated we can tune queue depth and batch sizing. We also support graceful degradation: if queue depth is exceeded, you can return cached responses or a lightweight fallback model.
[06:52] Sam W.: For our telemetry, will we get per-token latency and cost breakdowns?
[06:57] Samira Patel: Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route and per-model dashboards, plus traces for slow requests. We'll provide that data during the POC.
[07:07] Leah Kim: In terms of responsibilities, can we summarize who does what?
[07:10] Alex Chen: Sure — Redwood: POC infra and runbooks, sandbox accounts, benchmarks. Hyperion: traffic data, prompts, and internal stakeholders for compliance review. We'll exchange security docs.
[07:22] Priya Singh: One more on SSO and RBAC: can we integrate with our Okta and have role-level access to the console and keys?
[07:29] Samira Patel: Yes, SSO via SAML/Okta and fine-grained RBAC are supported on enterprise plans. We'll share the integration guide.
[07:36] Javier Morales: If we run private/on-prem, how do rollouts work? Is the control plane external?
[07:42] Samira Patel: For Private we have two deployment models: managed control plane (Redwood controls routing but customer-managed VPC) or fully air-gapped where you run the control plane too. For the managed control plane, rollouts and canaries are still via our Console; for air-gapped we provide admin tooling for local rollouts.
[07:58] Mike Torres: If we choose private and manage everything, would we still get the same fallback features?
[08:04] Samira Patel: Yes, but you'd need to run the fallback orchestration locally. We provide the orchestration blueprint and the binaries. Some advanced features like cross-region failover via Redwood control plane require managed mode.
[08:15] Alex Chen: Ok wrapping — let's do a quick recap and make sure next steps are clear.
[08:20] Leah Kim: Recap please.
[08:22] Alex Chen: POC scope: benchmark latency and failover scenarios, include region outage simulation, model degradation, and cache-warm strategies. Redwood to provide pricing, SOC2/security pack, and pre-warm guidance. Hyperion to provide traffic profiles and prompts. Schedule technical deep dive for SREs week of 2027-09-27.
[08:38] Samira Patel: I'll follow up with links: POC template, failure injection scripts, and the SOC2/security bundle.
[08:44] Mike Torres: Sounds good. One final ask — can you include an architecture diagram showing active-active dedicated pools across US-EU with routing and cache replication?
[08:53] Samira Patel: Yes, we'll include that as an attachment.
[08:56] Alex Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll email notes and next steps.
[09:00] Meeting ends.
